subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: She told me that she ___ the film the previous week.
explanation:
A past reporting verb shifts an earlier past action into the past perfect.
"the previous week" marks an action before the reporting time.

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: Hardly had we left the house when it ___ to rain.
explanation: "Hardly + had + past participle" is followed by "when + simple past".

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: I wish I ___ harder for the exam last year.
explanation:
A wish about the past takes the past perfect.
"last year" fixes the time in the past.

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: It is high time we ___ for the station.
explanation: "It is high time + subject" is followed by the simple past form with present meaning.

subject: english
question: Choose the correct verb: The quality of these mangoes ___ not good.
explanation: The verb agrees with the head noun "quality" (singular), not with "mangoes".

subject: english
question: Choose the correct verb: Either you or he ___ to blame.
explanation: With "either ... or", the verb agrees with the nearer subject ("he").

subject: english
question: Choose the correct verb: A large number of tourists ___ Pokhara every year.
explanation:
"A number of" means "many" and takes a plural verb.
"every year" calls for the simple present.

subject: english
question: Choose the correct verb: The Prime Minister, along with his ministers, ___ expected tomorrow.
explanation:
Phrases with "along with" do not change the number of the subject.
The subject "The Prime Minister" is singular.

subject: english
question: Choose the correct verb: The secretary and treasurer of the club ___ absent today.
explanation:
With one article before two nouns joined by "and", one person is meant.
So the verb is singular.

subject: english
question: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Please help me."
options: He said me to help him.
He requested me to help him.
He requested me to please help him.
He told me that please help him.
explanation:
Requests become "requested + object + to-infinitive"; "please" is dropped.
Pronouns change to suit the reporter.

subject: english
question: Change into indirect speech: She said, "I have finished my homework."
options: She said that she has finished her homework.
She said that she had finished my homework.
She said that she had finished her homework.
She said that I had finished her homework.
explanation:
Past reporting verb: present perfect becomes past perfect.
"I/my" change to "she/her".

subject: english
question: Change into indirect speech: He said, "What a beautiful view it is!"
options: He exclaimed what a beautiful view it is.
He said that what a beautiful view it was.
He asked how beautiful the view was.
He exclaimed that it was a very beautiful view.
explanation:
Exclamations use "exclaimed that"; "What a" becomes "very".
The tense shifts back: "is" becomes "was".

subject: english
question: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to the boy, "Did you break the window?"
options: The teacher asked the boy if he had broken the window.
The teacher asked the boy did he break the window.
The teacher asked the boy if he has broken the window.
The teacher said to the boy that he had broken the window.
explanation:
Yes/no questions use "asked + if/whether" with statement word order.
Simple past becomes past perfect.

subject: english
question: Change into indirect speech (reported a week later): He said, "I will come tomorrow."
options: He said that he will come tomorrow.
He said that he would come the next day.
He said that he will come the next day.
He said that I would come the next day.
explanation:
"will" becomes "would" after a past reporting verb.
Reported later, "tomorrow" becomes "the next day".

subject: english
question: Transform using "No sooner": As soon as he saw the police, the thief ran away.
options: No sooner had the thief seen the police when he ran away.
No sooner the thief saw the police than he ran away.
No sooner did the thief see the police than he ran away.
No sooner did the thief see the police then he ran away.
explanation: "No sooner" takes inverted word order and is paired with "than", never "when" or "then".

subject: english
question: Transform without changing the meaning: He is too weak to walk.
options: He is so weak that he can walk.
He is very weak that he cannot walk.
He is so weak to walk.
He is so weak that he cannot walk.
explanation: "too ... to" equals "so ... that + negative".

subject: english
question: Add the correct question tag: Let's go for a swim, ___?
explanation: A sentence beginning with "Let's" takes the tag "shall we".

subject: english
question: Transform into the comparative degree: Very few cities in Nepal are as large as Kathmandu.
options: Kathmandu is the largest city in Nepal.
Kathmandu is larger than most other cities in Nepal.
Kathmandu is larger than any other city in Nepal.
Kathmandu is not so large as most other cities in Nepal.
explanation:
"Very few ... as large as X" becomes "X is larger than most other ...".
"any other" would wrongly mean it is the largest of all.

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: If you had told me earlier, I ___ you.
explanation: Third conditional: "If + past perfect", "would have + past participle".

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: ___ he come, tell him to wait.
explanation: "Should" with inversion replaces "If" in a first-conditional clause: "Should he come" = "If he comes".

subject: english
question: In the sentence "He ran fast to catch the bus", the word "fast" is a(n):
explanation: "fast" modifies the verb "ran", telling how he ran, so it is an adverb.

subject: english
question: In the sentence "The poor need our help", the word "poor" is used as a:
explanation: "the + adjective" names a class of people and works as a plural noun (subject of "need").

subject: english
question: Change into passive voice: She will finish the report by Friday.
options: The report would be finished by her by Friday.
The report will be finish by her by Friday.
The report will be finished by her by Friday.
The report will been finished by her by Friday.
explanation: Future simple passive: will + be + past participle.

subject: english
question: Change into passive voice: We must protect our forests.
options: Our forests must have been protected.
explanation:
Modal passive: modal + be + past participle.
The agent "by us" is usually omitted.

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: You had better ___ a doctor.
explanation: "had better" is followed by the bare infinitive (without "to").

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: I am looking forward to ___ you.
explanation: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so a gerund follows.

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: He avoided ___ the question.
explanation: "avoid" is always followed by a gerund.

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: She made me ___ the whole story again.
explanation: Active "make + object" takes the bare infinitive.

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: ___ his work, he went home.
explanation: A perfect participle (having + past participle) shows an action completed before the main action.

subject: english
question: Which of these sentences uses the participle correctly?
options: Walking along the road, a snake was seen by me.
Walking along the road, I saw a snake.
Walking along the road, a snake bit me.
Walking along the road, the snake was seen.
explanation:
The subject of the main clause must be the doer of the participle.
Otherwise the participle "dangles".

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: She has been absent ___ school for three days.
explanation: "absent" takes the preposition "from".

subject: english
question: Fill in the blank: He is married ___ a doctor.
explanation: "married" takes "to": be married to someone.

subject: english
question: Choose the phrase with the correct articles.
explanation:
"hour" begins with a vowel sound (silent h): "an".
"half" begins with a consonant sound: "a".

subject: english
question: Fill in the blanks: ___ rich should help ___ poor.
explanation: "the + adjective" refers to a whole class of people.

subject: english
question: What is the pattern of the sentence "They elected him captain."?
explanation: "him" is the object and "captain" is an object complement describing him.

subject: english
question: Which sentence has the pattern S + V + IO + DO?
options: She put the pen on the table.
She gave her brother a pen.
explanation: "her brother" is the indirect object (receiver) and "a pen" the direct object.

subject: english
question: Which word has a different vowel sound from the others?
explanation:
"blood" has the short vowel as in "cup".
The others have the long vowel as in "too".

subject: english
question: Which of these words has a vowel sound different from the rest?
explanation:
"heart" has the vowel of "car".
The others have the vowel of "her".

subject: english
question: Pick the word whose vowel sound differs from the other three.
explanation:
"bread" has the short vowel of "bed".
The others have the vowel of "day".

subject: english
question: In which word is "ch" pronounced differently from the others?
explanation:
In "chemistry", "ch" is pronounced as "k".
In the others it is the sound in "chin".

subject: english
question: Which word has the same middle consonant sound as "measure"?
explanation:
"measure" and "pleasure" share the sound in "vision".
"pressure" has the "sh" sound, "messenger" the "j" sound, "lesson" an "s".

subject: english
question: In which word is the letter "b" silent?
explanation:
In "doubt" the "b" is not pronounced.
It is pronounced in the other words.

subject: english
question: In which word is "th" pronounced as in "this"?
explanation:
The verb "breathe" has the voiced "th" of "this".
The others have the voiceless "th" of "thin".

subject: english
question: How many syllables are there in the word "examination"?
explanation: ex-am-i-na-tion: five syllables.

subject: english
question: Which word has three syllables?
explanation: beau-ti-ful has three; gar-den two, un-der-stand-ing four, cat one.

subject: english
question: Which word has the stress on the second syllable?
explanation:
be-GIN is stressed on the second syllable.
The others are stressed on the first.

subject: english
question: Which word has the stress on the first syllable?
explanation: PHO-to-graph; pho-TO-gra-pher; pho-to-GRAPH-ic; po-TA-to.

subject: english
question: In which sentence is "record" stressed on the second syllable?
options: He keeps a record of his expenses.
explanation:
As a noun, "record" is stressed on the first syllable; as a verb, on the second.
Only the first sentence uses it as a verb.

subject: english
question: Which word has the stress on the third syllable?
explanation:
en-gi-NEER; EN-gine; en-JOY-ment; EN-er-gy.
Words ending in "-eer" are stressed on that ending.

subject: english
question: Which word has the same vowel sound as "boat"?
explanation:
"boat" and "home" share the vowel of "go".
"cot", "bought" and "boot" have other vowels.

subject: english
question: Read: "Ramesh had saved money for months to buy a bicycle. When he saw his neighbour's house destroyed by the flood, he gave all his savings to the family." What does the passage suggest about Ramesh?
options: He was paid to help the family.
explanation:
He gave up his own savings to help people in need.
This shows generosity.

subject: english
question: Read: "The village had no electricity until 2015. Now every house has solar panels, and children can study at night." According to the passage, what has changed in the village?
options: Children no longer go to school.
Children can now study after dark.
explanation: The passage says that solar panels now let children study at night.

subject: english
question: Read: "Despite repeated warnings from experts, the factory continued to dump waste into the river. Within a year, most of the fish had disappeared." The word "despite" is closest in meaning to:
explanation: "despite" means "in spite of"; the factory ignored the warnings.

subject: english
question: Read: "The new manager was reticent at meetings; he listened carefully but rarely shared his own views." Here "reticent" means:
explanation: The clue "rarely shared his own views" shows he was reserved, not inclined to speak.

subject: english
question: Read: "After the long drought, the rain was a welcome relief, and the parched fields turned green again within weeks." Here "parched" means:
explanation: The clue "long drought" shows the fields were very dry.

subject: english
question: Read: "Scientists once believed the disease was incurable. However, a new vaccine has reduced cases by ninety per cent in five years." What is the main idea?
options: Scientists have stopped studying the disease.
The disease has always been easy to cure.
A disease once thought incurable is now being controlled.
explanation: "However" contrasts the old belief with the vaccine's success.

subject: english
question: Read: "Sita's plan to start a small bakery seemed feasible: she had the skills, a little capital and a shop near the school." Here "feasible" means:
explanation:
The listed resources show the plan could be carried out.
"feasible" means possible to do.

subject: english
question: Read: "The old bridge was not demolished; instead it was renovated, and it now looks as good as new." What happened to the bridge?
options: It was replaced by a new bridge.
explanation:
"renovated" means repaired and restored.
"not demolished" rules out pulling it down.

subject: english
question: Read: "Though the team lost the final, the coach praised the players for their tenacity, as they had fought until the last minute." Here "tenacity" means:
explanation: The clue "fought until the last minute" shows determination.

subject: english
question: Read: "Many people in the hills walk for hours to fetch water. A new pipeline will bring water to their doorsteps next year, saving both time and effort." What will the pipeline do?
options: Take water away from the hills.
Save people the long walk to fetch water.
explanation: Water at the doorstep means people no longer need to walk for hours.
